chunks: Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If good character were a visible creature, there would be nothing more beautiful in creation than it; and if evil character were a visible creature, there would be nothing uglier in creation than it. Verily, Allah causes the servant with good character to attain the station of one who fasts and stands in prayer.'

key_terms.الصَّائِمِ الْقَائِمِ: The fasting one who stands (in night prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of having good character in Islam according to the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Ahwazi’s *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the Shia emphasis on *husn al-khuluq* as a tangible spiritual reality that can elevate a believer to the rank of *al-sa'im al-qaim* (the fasting one who prays at night). By contrasting the visible beauty of good character with the ugliness of its opposite, it highlights moral conduct as a primary metric of piety, complementing ritual worship. This aligns with the Imami tradition where ethical refinement is often viewed as the fruit of deep spiritual devotion.
